Resolves #20070

A tab released on an edge band of its own pane now lands the split the hover previewed. Before the fix, nothing landed and the dock reported an abandoned gesture.

`DragAffordances#onDrop` re-derived the release preview with the drag's own tabs node filtered out (`zones.filter(zone => zone.nodeId !== sourceNodeId)`), but `previewAt`, which drives the hover, reads every zone, the drag's own included. The release now reads the zones the hover read. Only an own-node `tab-into` still commits nothing, because the within-toolbar reorder already landed it, which is the exemption `reportUnlanded` already makes. The docblock's old reason ("the within-toolbar reorder already handled them") was only ever true of that interior.

Evidence: L3 (headless Chromium Neural Link e2e on `apps/workstation`, 4× CPU throttle + unit) → L3 required (a pointer gesture on the dock). Residual: AC-4, Residual-Owner: #20022.

It is red on `dev` source and green at head. "a tab-into of its own zone is the reorder's…" stays green. |
| AC-2 | Outside-CI (Neural Link specs are not in the CI selection): `WorkstationOwnPaneEdgeDropNL.spec` drags a `heavy-tabs` tab to that pane's lower band under a 4× throttle. On `dev` it failed 2/2 with the operator's signature (`DragCoordinator: a pointer drag of alerts ended in no-operation although its window accepted preview:alerts:heavy-tabs:edge-bottom`) and no split. At head it passed 3/3: a vertical split with the tab alone below the others. |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: "the own zone's bottom chip lands the same split as its bottom band" is green on `dev` and at head. The chip path already kept self-targets; both paths now agree. |
| AC-4 | Post-merge, below. |

## Deltas from ticket
- **The #19869 arm is converted.** "a release that lands nothing where the hover showed a split of its own zone reports it" pinned the very abandonment this PR removes, so it becomes AC-1's arm.
- **`no-operation` keeps its own red.** A new stubbed arm, "a release that infers nothing where the hover showed a preview reports it", proves that terminal still reports.
- **The `other-operation` arm now uses call order.** It used to tell the drop's inference from the hover's read by the filtered zones; now it does so by call order.
